deferred_arguments.rule: Each placeholder below stands, inside one single-quoted word of a command's shell member, for a value that is taken mechanically from the named source. The Director replaces every occurrence of the placeholder text in that member and nothing else; the values hold no quote. A 64-hex value is 64 lowercase hexadecimal characters; a root is a path that matches the stated pattern. The checker verifies each replaced word against its source (equals_freeze_sha256, equals_sha256_of, equals_from or the stated prefix).

launch.rule: MH's freeze 002 launch (FR-01 (a) and (b), FR2-03 and FR2-05), applied unchanged to MR's wrapper
launch.before_p00: Immediately before P00, in one read, the Director compares the SHA-256 of <F>/FREEZE-001.json and of <F>/SHA256SUMS.txt with the freeze review record's values, and the wrapper's with 9154f181cfa7c8648c21b31a1f309af43f9b2b5046df1656a124a4b6b55e07a7 (HR-08), using /usr/bin/shasum, and records the result. S7 begins only if all three are equal (MH's FR2-05).
launch.command: Every command runs as its shell member alone, read raw with jq -r, with only its deferred placeholders replaced. Nothing is prepended or appended, so zsh -c runs one simple command and the wrapper leads its group. It goes to the shell tool in background mode with no tool timeout: one call per command, never retried.
launch.timer: In the same message, as the second call, the Director passes the command's timer_shell, read the same way and passed alone, also in background mode with no tool timeout. It is MH's timer template with the command's exit file and limits.outer_bound_s. It exits at the first of two events: the exit file exists ('bound-timer: exit-file ...', status 0), or more than outer_bound_s whole epoch seconds have passed ('bound-timer: outer-bound ...', status 1). It starts only shell builtins, /bin/date and /bin/sleep, and writes nothing.
launch.after: The Director goes on when the command's background task has ended and its timer has printed 'exit-file'; it then reads the exit file and applies the command's classification and stop_rules. 'outer-bound' while the command's task still runs: the overrun procedure. 'no-clock', or any other timer output or status: a PLAN deviation of this freeze's own tool; the Director records it, waits for the command's task without a bound, runs the command's listing and probe as frozen, and stops S7. A timer line printed after the task ended has effect only as FR2-03 (b) says: when the command record's end_epoch_s - start_epoch_s is not above outer_bound_s, an 'outer-bound' line had no effect. A wrapper exit of 90 leaves no exit file: the command did not start (a PLAN deviation; stop S7). Exits 91 and 92 come after the exit file: the command ran once and its record is missing (UNKNOWN; stop S7).
launch.order_and_approval: Each launch message holds exactly two calls: the command first and its timer second. If either waits for an approval or is refused, the launch has deviated: a command that did not start did not run, and S7 stops before it (class HOST, the Director's executor), with no retry; a command that started is waited for, its listing and probe run as frozen, and S7 stops after them (MH's FR2-03 (a)).
launch.director_starts: Recorded, not bounded: one zsh per tool call; each timer's /bin/date about once a second and its /bin/sleep; one jq per member read; /usr/bin/shasum and /usr/bin/cut for each deferred digest; and inside each wrapper call /bin/sh, /usr/bin/env, /usr/bin/jq (about 4), /usr/bin/shasum (3), /usr/bin/cut (3), /bin/date (2), /usr/bin/perl (3), /usr/sbin/sysctl (2) and /usr/bin/stat (2) (MH's FR2-06). None starts Node or the framework interpreter.
launch.dash_b: Every start of the framework interpreter in this freeze carries -B on its command line (N-09, D-P4). The Director's own reads use no interpreter. The owner is asked to keep every other user of that interpreter (the launchd job of MH's PR-03 and the other agent application of PR-02) from starting it without -B, or to pause them, from P00 to the end of S8 (HR-04).

overrun.rule: MH's FR-01 (c) six steps, with MR's records. A command that ends at its bound may be reported as an overrun, never the reverse.
steps: 1. Record the overrun with its UTC time and epoch seconds. The command's outcome is UNKNOWN. Start the command's own timer_shell a second time (MH's A-3).

2. R1: run R1.N (it reads names only). If it exits 0, run R1.O with its printed root, which probes every candidate pair of R1's three cases; a pair whose records do not exist is reported, not refused. Any other command (R2, a tool, a checker) has no supervised child with a recorded pair, so step 2 is empty for it.

3. Run R1.S<k> once for each target of R1.O in state 'present, identity established', where target j-1 is case j in the order Q01-positive, Q03-positive, Q01-changed-reference, confirmed by the target's pair.started.path (MH's FR2-01). Send nothing for any other state.
4. Send nothing to the wrapper, the tool's task, the driver, its steps or any of their groups: no record establishes their identity (FC-P1, FC-P2).

5. Wait for the wrapper to exit. Then run the command's listing (R1.L or R2.L), for R1 also R1.I, R1.F and, if R1.F exits 0, R1.P; write the capture record (failure_capture.record) and stop S7. No collector, comparator, reader, audit or X/Y/Z check runs.
6. If the second timer ends first, tell the owner, keep waiting and start nothing.

r1.pairs: <root>/provider-ledgers/<case>/preflight.json and started.json (FAILURE-CAPTURE FC-P2, the provider row)

overrun.other: R2, the tools and the checkers: steps 1, 4, 5 and 6 only.
limits: A start recorded after R1.N reads the root is probed only after the wrapper exits (step 5, R1.P).
A start between its preflight.json and its started.json cannot be named.
FC-P5: a descendant that moved to another process group or session is not found by the group probe.

rules: 1. P00's exit file other than '0\n', or the before_p00 comparison unequal: S7 does not begin.
2. P01 or D02 not exit 0 with state MET: R1 does not start. P02, P03 or D01 not exit 0: stop; D02 records the predicates.

3. A command's exit status outside its allowed_exit_statuses, or a missing exit file or command record: its outcome is UNKNOWN; FAILURE-CAPTURE section 6; S7 stops after the steps that its classification names; no retry.

3a. The sequence after a run. When R1's wrapper has exited without an overrun, the Director runs R1.L, R1.I, R1.F, R1.P, R1.C, R1.K, R1.A, R1.R, R1.M, R1.X, R1.Y and R1.Z in this order, whatever R1's outcome. A step whose frozen input file does not exist (the unit log after a preparation refusal; the cohort root when R1.F exits 1, for R1.P, R1.A and R1.R; the audit's output, for R1.R) is not started and is recorded as NOT_RUN in the capture record. R1.M, R1.X, R1.Y and R1.Z always run. After R2's wrapper has exited the same holds for R2.L, R2.I, R2.C, R2.K, R2.V, R2.M, R2.X and R2.Y, and Q01, Q01.X and Q04 follow.
4. R1.X or R1.Z NOT_MET: R2 does not start; S7 stops after R1.Y and R1.Z. R2.X NOT_MET: S7 stops after R2.Y, Q01, Q01.X and Q04.

5. R1.Y or R2.Y NOT_MET: FINDINGS, recorded; they never stop S7 (MR-PLAN section 9). A NOT_MET predicate of MC23 means that R1 is not qualified and MR is unmet; R2 still runs when R1.X and R1.Z are MET, because R2 is independent evidence for MC22 and the symlinked-directory comparison and starts no Node.

6. A probe target (R1.P) in any state other than absent: UNKNOWN; FC-P6 for an established identity only; S7 stops after R1.M, R1.X, R1.Y and R1.Z. FR2-02's reading applies to a pair whose records do not exist when the ledger shows that the start never happened.
7. An overrun: the overrun procedure; S7 stops.
8. A boot change (any command record's boot.before or boot.after other than the frozen UUID): the attempt ends (FC-R5); MR's S4 starts again with new records.
9. Nothing is retried (FC-R1, FC-R2). A corrected attempt needs a new attempt ID, a freeze that states the cause, and its review (FC-R3, MR-PLAN section 9). The earlier attempt is retained.
